extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, Florida stakeholders, and MyFLRules users who want to follow Florida state rulemaking, submit comments, or subscribe to rulemaking notices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for members of the public and stakeholders on how to find rules open for comment, submit one-time or saved comments, create a MyFLRules account, subscribe/unsubscribe to alerts, and understand basic Florida rulemaking definitions and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period length
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, a proposed notice is open for 21 days for public comments, starting from the day it was published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding rules open for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: To get a list of all the rules currently open for comments, select the 'Rules Open for Comments' tab; find the individual rule and select the number under the notice ID column; then locate the COMMENTS section on the notice's page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: (1) Click 'Rules Open for Comments' tab; (2) choose a specific notice by its ID; (3) use the COMMENTS section on that notice's page to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send a one-time comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Select 'Send a one-time comment to the Agency' and click the 'Make Comment' button to submit a one-time comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system requires a subject and your comment. You may optionally provide a title, first and last name, and e-mail address. Providing name/email does not guarantee agency contact. Click 'Submit Comment' to complete. If you want to save your comment, you must be logged in (create a profile).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate with the Agency (saved comments & agency replies)
rubrics_metrics.description: To save comments and receive agency replies, select 'Communicate with the Agency with saved comments and agency replies' and use the 'Make Comment' form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must be logged in (Subscriber Login). On the 'Make Comment' form choose your role, give your comments a subject, and write your comments in the Comment box. Login uses your MyFLRules username and password.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to be contacted by an agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing your name and e-mail address on a one-time comment does not guarantee that you will be contacted by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want someone from the agency to contact you, you must log in and select 'Communicate with the Agency' (i.e., use saved comments and agency replies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscribe for Notifications (MyFLRules alerts)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can subscribe to e-mail notifications for notices submitted by agencies to receive regular updates on rulemaking, public meetings and other activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workflow: (1) Create a MyFLRules account; (2) log in; (3) go to 'Advanced Search'; (4) select 'Search in the Florida Administrative Register' checkbox; (5) select Department Name and division(s) to follow (hold Ctrl or Command to select multiple); (6) click 'Search'; (7) at bottom of results click 'Save to My Alert Profile'; (8) enter a Profile Name and click 'Save To My Profile'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select multiple divisions in Advanced Search
rubrics_metrics.description: When choosing divisions to follow, you may select multiple divisions by holding down the Control (Ctrl) key, or the Command key on a Mac.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubscribe for Notifications (delete alert profile)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are able to delete alert profiles so you no longer receive alert emails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: log in; click on a profile name to delete; click 'Delete This Profile'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a MyFLRules account (Subscriber sign-up)
rubrics_metrics.description: To sign up, go to the Subscriber sign-up page, select a title, enter your name and e-mail address (email is your login), and choose a password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Password must be 4 to 20 characters (letters or numbers only). After sign-up the Subscriber Sign-up page will confirm your subscription. Benefits of an account: save and track comments on proposed rules and other notices, receive e-mail alerts when new notices are published, save searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is Rulemaking? (basic definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking is defined as the adoption, amendment or repeal of a rule. In its simplest form it consists of drafting the rule text, providing notice to the public, accepting public comment and filing the rule for adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking can involve many more steps and become more complicated than the basic sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is a Rule? (Chapter 120 statutory definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per Chapter 120, Florida Statutes: 'Rule means each agency statement of general applicability that implements, interprets, or prescribes law or policy or describes the procedure or practice requirements of an agency and includes any form which imposes any requirement or solicits any information not specifically required by statute or by an existing rule.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term also includes the amendment or repeal of a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is the Florida Administrative Code (FAC)?
rubrics_metrics.description: The Florida Administrative Code is the official compilation of administrative rules for the state of Florida. The Department of State oversees publishing the FAC and updates it weekly.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is the Florida Administrative Register (FAR)?
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAR is a daily publication giving the public current information about the status of rules moving through the rulemaking process, including proposed rules, emergency rules, and notices of change, corrections and withdrawals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Register also includes notices of agency public meetings, workshops and hearings, and miscellaneous actions required to be published by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Rule Development (FAR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of Rule Development are required to be published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Proposed Rules (FAR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of Proposed Rules are required to be published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Change, Correction and Withdrawal (FAR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of Change, Correction and Withdrawal are required to be published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Rules (FAR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency Rules must be published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions and Dispositions Regarding Rule Variance and Waiver (FAR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of petitions and dispositions regarding rule variance and waiver must be published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Meetings, Workshops and Public Hearings (FAR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of agency meetings, workshops and public hearings must be published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Petitions and Dispositions Regarding Declaratory Statements (FAR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of petitions and dispositions regarding declaratory statements must be published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Petitions and Dispositions Regarding Non-rule Policy Changes (FAR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of petitions and dispositions regarding non-rule policy changes must be published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcements and Objection Reports of the Joint Administrative Procedures Committee (FAR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements and objection reports of the Joint Administrative Procedures Committee are required in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices Regarding Bids, Proposals and Purchasing (FAR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices regarding bids, proposals and purchasing must be published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Intent to Adopt Rules (statutory cross-references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of Intent to Adopt rules pursuant to Sections 120.54(6), 120.54(1)(i)2., and 403.8055, Florida Statute, are required to be published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Invalidation of a Proposed or Effective Rule (FAR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of invalidation of a proposed or effective rule must be published in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing law: Chapter 120 and Chapter 1-1 (rulemaking authorities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter 120, Florida Statutes (Administrative Procedure Act) sets forth the rulemaking procedures agencies must follow. The Department of State has adopted Chapter 1-1, Florida Administrative Code, to interpret, implement and make specific the requirements of Chapter 120.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency rulemaking authority requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency must have a grant of rulemaking authority and a specific law to be implemented before it may draft, amend, or repeal a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may adopt only rules that implement or interpret the specific powers and duties granted by the enabling statute. An agency does not have authority to adopt a rule solely because it is reasonably related to the purpose of the enabling legislation, to avoid being arbitrary and capricious, or because it is within the agency's class of powers and duties. Agencies cannot implement general legislative intent or policy as the sole basis for rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference material & incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rule makes reference to a form, document, or related item, it must be 'incorporated by reference' into the rule. Reference materials may include ordinances, standards, specifications, maps, graphs, charts, reports or similar materials generally available to affected persons and published by governmental agencies or recognized professional organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any forms, including instructions, which solicit information or impose requirements not already required by statute or existing rule and which are used by an agency in its dealings with the public shall be incorporated by reference in the rule if it meets the definition of a 'rule.'

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail addresses are public records (caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Florida law, e-mail addresses are public records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not want your e-mail address released in response to a public records request, do not send electronic mail to this entity; instead contact the office by phone or in writing.
